title: History survives removal; re-enrol anchors from last completion
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in as an Owner/Admin, or a user with "Settings Service" enabled, on the build under test. The Maintenance Reminders feature is on (behind the maintenance_reminders flag).
  2. An asset with completed maintenance cycles that is removed from a schedule (or whose schedule is archived), then enrolled again later. Seed: enrol an asset, complete a cycle or two, then remove it (or archive the schedule).
custom_steps:
1. Remove the schedule from the asset (or archive the schedule) and check the asset's cycle history.
  2. Enrol the asset on a schedule again and check where each service anchors from.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Removing a schedule from an asset does not destroy history - cycles belong to the asset-and-service pair.
  • Applying a schedule afterwards anchors each service from the last completion of the same-named service on that asset, otherwise from now.
  • Archiving unenrols without destroying history, so enrolling again later anchors from the last completion.
  • A new regulatory requirement is the known weak point: the shop must apply the schedule again per unit and nothing warns it.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-3780; story SV-10563 (S6, Edit and archive a schedule); Chunk 1 MR spec (Confluence 886931488), S6; read 29 Sep 2026. Source-verified 29 September 2026; not yet build-verified.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S6-E1: “Removing a schedule from an asset does not destroy history. Cycles belong to the asset and service pair”
  • S6-E2: “Applying a new schedule afterwards anchors each service from the last completion of the service of the same name on that asset, otherwise from now”
  • S6-E4: “Archiving unenrols without destroying history. Each asset keeps its completed cycles ... so enrolling it again later anchors from the last completion”
  • S6-E3: “A new regulatory requirement is the known weak point. The shop must apply the schedule again per unit and nothing warns it”
